extractions.description: Empirical cognitive-neuroscience study using behavioral testing, high-density EEG, multivariate decoding, representational similarity analysis, and pretrained neural-network representations. The extraction catalogs only its computational artifacts and compute configurations.

type.quote: We collected a large dataset of high-density electrophysiological (EEG) recordings from PS and neurotypicals while they completed a one-back task
type.justification: The paper reports newly collected observations and computational analyses, so it is empirical.

name.quote: Here, we report an investigation of the neural computations involved in the processing of faces and objects of patient PS, a well-documented case of pure acquired prosopagnosia
name.justification: The study directly advances research on acquired prosopagnosia.

name.quote: thereby offering a window into the neural computations at play in patient PS’s deficits
name.justification: The paper characterizes neural computations and dynamics from EEG and computational models.

name.quote: Understanding the very nature of defective perceptual representations offers new routes for patient rehabilitation.
name.justification: The paper addresses the neuropsychology of impaired perceptual representations in a brain-lesioned patient.

name.quote: We found reduced neural decoding of face identity around the N170 window in PS
name.justification: Face identity and face-recognition processing are central claims addressed by the paper.

name.quote: Here, we take into account these temporal and computational aspects of brain processes by investigating prosopagnosia with fine-grained temporal recordings of brain activity (high-density electroencephalography; EEG), machine learning, and a proven multivariate method
name.justification: Machine learning is used as an analysis setting rather than advanced as a field.

name.quote: We used a pre-trained AlexNet (Krizhevsky et al., 2012) as one model of the visual computations along the ventral stream
